seoTitle: The Pitt Test: Which Character Are You? (12 Questions)
metaDescription: Take The Pitt test: 12 everyday questions reveal whether you're Robby, Dana, Langdon, Santos, Mohan, Mel King, Whitaker or McKay. Get your full character breakdown.
intro: Are you the one who always stays late, the one who takes charge when everyone panics, or the one who gets it right but takes their time? Answer 12 everyday questions about work, pressure and the people you look after, and find out which Pitt character you are.

characters.name: Dr. Robby
characters.title: The One Who Always Stays
characters.summary: Dedicated, calm and carrying far more than anyone knows. You look after everyone, except yourself.
description: Like Dr. Michael "Robby" Robinavitch, you're the one everyone leans on. He's the senior attending physician in the Pittsburgh emergency room, guiding his residents and students through every shift.
You hold it together for everyone else. Robby is still carrying the trauma of the COVID pandemic and the death of his mentor, but he keeps showing up.
Your problem is stopping. Robby keeps putting off the break he badly needs, because there's always one more patient.
characters.flaw: You take care of everyone else and run yourself into the ground.
characters.signature: Twelve hours into a shift, still teaching, still staying for one more patient.
characters.clashReason: they'd never leave work, and they'd expect you to stay too

characters.name: Dana Evans
characters.title: The Charge Nurse
characters.summary: Tough, funny and completely unshakeable. You run the place, and you've got a soft spot for everyone in it.
description: Like Dana, you're the one who actually keeps everything running. She's the day-shift charge nurse, and nobody in the ER gets anything past her.
You put on a strong front, but you care deeply. Dana mentors the young staff, fights for her patients and keeps a close eye on Robby.
You always come back. After Dana was punched by a patient, she thought about leaving, but as she puts it, she's like an old trail horse who always finds her way home.
characters.flaw: You're so busy looking after everyone that nobody notices when you're hurting.
characters.signature: A clipboard, a no-nonsense look and a quiet word for whoever needs it.
characters.clashReason: they'd boss you around, and they'd be right

characters.name: Dr. Langdon
characters.title: The Confident Charmer
characters.summary: Quick, charming and very good at what you do, but you hide your struggles behind that confidence.
description: Like Dr. Frank Langdon, you're quick-witted and self-assured. He's a talented senior resident who loves the adrenaline of the ER.
But you hide things when they go wrong. Langdon was secretly stealing medication to cope, and when Robby found out, he was sent home.
You know what it takes to earn back trust. Langdon went to rehab and came back, starting at the bottom and proving himself one patient at a time.
strengths: Works hard to make things right
characters.flaw: You'd rather hide a problem than admit you need help.
characters.signature: A cocky grin, a fast diagnosis and a lot to prove.
characters.clashReason: they'd act like everything's fine when it clearly isn't

characters.name: Dr. Santos
characters.title: The Blunt Overachiever
characters.summary: Ambitious, blunt and secretly kind. You say exactly what you think, and you don't care who likes it.
description: Like Dr. Trinity Santos, you're here to be the best. She started as a cocky, ambitious intern who didn't mind stepping on toes.
You say what nobody else will. Santos reported Langdon's drug problem when others kept quiet, and she paid a price for it with her colleagues.
Under the attitude, you're kinder than you let on. Santos let Whitaker live with her when he had nowhere to go, while teasing him and calling him "Huckleberry".
characters.flaw: You'd rather be right than be liked, and sometimes you're neither.
characters.signature: An eye roll, a sharp comment and a spare room for a friend who needs it.
characters.clashReason: they'd tell you exactly what you did wrong, in front of everyone

characters.name: Dr. Mohan
characters.title: The Thorough One
characters.summary: Careful, compassionate and determined to do things properly, even when everyone wants you to hurry up.
description: Like Dr. Samira Mohan, you believe in doing things right. She takes the time to really listen to her patients, even in a packed emergency room.
That gets you teased. Robby nicknamed her "Slow-Mo" because she takes so long with each patient, and learning to be faster without losing her care has been her biggest challenge.
You doubt yourself more than you should. Mohan is a very good doctor who's still learning to believe it.
characters.flaw: You worry so much about getting it perfect that you forget you're already good.
characters.signature: Sitting at a patient's bedside, listening, while the waiting room fills up.
characters.clashReason: they'd take forever to do the thing you needed done right now

characters.name: Dr. Mel King
characters.title: The Honest Heart
characters.summary: Kind, direct and deeply empathetic. You see people clearly and you treat everyone with care.
description: Like Dr. Mel King, you connect with people in a way others don't. She's a resident who treats every patient like a person, not a case.
You're refreshingly honest. Mel says what she means and means what she says, and people trust her for it.
Family is everything to you. Mel is devoted to her twin sister, Becca, who is autistic, and their bond is one of the sweetest things in the show.
characters.flaw: You feel other people's pain so deeply that it wears you out.
characters.signature: A gentle, honest explanation and a patient who finally feels understood.
characters.clashReason: they'd say the honest thing you didn't want to hear

characters.name: Dr. Whitaker
characters.title: The Underdog
characters.summary: Gentle, earnest and always trying his best. You get knocked down a lot, but you get back up and surprise everyone.
description: Like Dr. Dennis Whitaker, you're the sweet, slightly awkward one who's always trying hard. He started as a naive medical student, and plenty went wrong on his first day.
Life hasn't made it easy for you. Whitaker was secretly homeless while studying, until Santos let him stay with her.
But you grow into it. By season two Whitaker is a doctor with sharp instincts, and he's mentoring the new students himself.
characters.flaw: You don't give yourself enough credit.
characters.signature: A nervous smile, a lot of apologies and a save nobody expected.
characters.clashReason: they'd be far too nice to tell you what they really think

characters.name: Dr. McKay
characters.title: The Second Chance
characters.summary: Grounded, caring and quietly determined. You've been through a lot, and it's made you kinder, not harder.
description: Like Dr. Cassie McKay, you've taken a longer road than most. She became a resident in her forties, while raising her young son, Harrison, as a single mother.
You don't judge people, because you know life can go wrong. McKay wears an ankle monitor under her scrubs, and she's working hard to build a better life.
You're calm and capable. McKay has seen enough of life to stay steady when others panic, and her patients can feel it.
characters.flaw: You keep your past so hidden that people don't really know you.
characters.signature: Scrubs pulled over an ankle monitor, and a calm voice in a chaotic room.
characters.clashReason: they'd keep their whole life a mystery

questions.text: You're the newest person on a busy team. In your first week you...

options.text: Make sure everyone knows you're the best new hire
Try really hard, get a few things wrong, and apologise a lot
Do everything properly, even if it makes you the slowest
Get on with it quietly. You've got nothing to prove

questions.text: A coworker is obviously struggling but insists they're fine. You...

options.text: Pull them aside and tell them to take five
Check on them, even though you're running on empty yourself
Tell a manager. Someone has to
Ask them straight out if they're okay, and mean it

questions.text: Five minutes before you're due to leave, something urgent comes in. You...

options.text: Stay. You always stay
Take it, and give it all the time it needs
Jump in. You love the adrenaline
Hand it to the next shift. Nobody works well exhausted

questions.text: After a brutal week, how do you recharge?

options.text: Out with friends, cracking jokes all night
A quiet evening with someone you love and a long chat
Loud music, drinks and zero feelings
A glass of wine, feet up, phone off

questions.text: You make a mistake that could have really hurt someone. You...

options.text: Hide it and hope you can fix it before anyone notices
Go over it again and again in your head for weeks
Own it in front of everyone, and make sure they learn from it
Tell the person honestly and apologise

questions.text: People at work say you're "too slow" or "too different". You...

options.text: Keep doing it your way. Being thorough matters
Calmly explain why you do things the way you do
Ignore it. You've been through much worse
Take it on the chin and try even harder

questions.text: You want a hobby that has nothing to do with work. You go for...

options.text: Gardening. Something calm that actually grows
Something competitive. You play to win
Something detailed you can get completely lost in
Anything fast: climbing, surfing, the more adrenaline the better

questions.text: A friend suddenly has nowhere to live. You...

options.text: Let them crash with you, and tease them about it every day
Offer your sofa, and feel awkward that you can't do more
Make some calls and find them somewhere proper to stay
Take them in without a second thought. You know how fast life can go wrong

questions.text: Someone badly breaks your trust, then asks for another chance. You...

options.text: Give them one, but watch them closely
No. You were right about them from the start
Tell them exactly how things are going to work from now on
Say yes. You know what it's like to need one

questions.text: Everyone around you starts to panic. You...

options.text: Take charge. Everyone gets a job, right now
Stay calm on the outside, whatever's happening inside
Freeze for a second, then surprise everyone
Stay steady. You've seen worse, and it shows

questions.text: You're a doctor in a busy emergency room, and you suspect a colleague you like is stealing painkillers. You...

options.text: Report it. Patients come first
Confront them privately before anything else
Ask them gently if they're okay
Tell someone senior, and feel awful about it

questions.text: You're a doctor in an emergency room. A patient's family is shouting at you because everything is taking too long. You...

options.text: Step in, calm them down and set some ground rules
Sit with them and listen. They're scared
Charm them. A joke, a smile, problem solved
Explain exactly what you're doing and why it takes time
